title: Ops Bridge Log — Shift Crew Notes (Nov 09 2027)
content:
Purpose:
Daily/weekly composite from the Ops Bridge shift crew (night->day handoff, Nov 09 2027). This doc is intended to capture the incidents we saw, SLO signal snapshots, immediate mitigation work, runbook edits, and action items for follow-up. Use this in the on-call handoff call and for the weekly SRE sync.

Summary (top-level):
- Shift window: 22:00 UTC (Nov 08) -> 06:00 UTC (Nov 09).
- Active incidents: 1 Sev2 (partial tokenization latency regression across europe-west region).
- SLOs impacted: Text-generation tail latency SLO (95th percentile) briefly breached in eu-west for ~45 minutes; overall error-rate SLO unaffected.
- Customer-facing impact: A few Dedicated customers reported increased response latency; no backend 5xx rates. CS ticket backlog spiked (10 new tickets) but no escalations to Sales.
- Runbook edits made: tokenization-latency-playbook v1.2 (small clarifications and telemetry links).

Incident: EU Tokenization Latency Regression (Sev2)
- Detection: Automated latency escalator alerted at 23:14 UTC when gen-text 95p for eu-west exceeded 350ms (target 250ms). Alert route: Pager->Ops Bridge.
- Scope: Affected nodes: gw-eu-*-pool-3 (approx 18% of EU serving capacity). Estimated affected customer sessions: 220 active requests during window.
- Timeline:
  - 23:14 UTC: Alert triggered (R-INF-1723).
  - 23:20 UTC: Ops Bridge triage: confirmed 95p latency increase and correlation with a spike in tokenizer microservice CPU.
  - 23:28 UTC: Canary traffic re-routed to alt-model-quant variant for critical customers -> immediate 20% reduction in observed 95p latency on canary.
  - 23:40 UTC: Identified recent infra deploy to tokenizer autoscaler (PR: infra/pull/287) that increased pod density but removed a CPU request guard, allowing burst scheduling to overcommit host CPUs.
  - 00:05 UTC: Short-term mitigation: scale-down autoscaler config rollback applied to gw-eu-*-pool-3 (R-INF-1730).
  - 00:26 UTC: 95p returned under SLO threshold for eu-west; alert recovered.
  - 00:45 UTC: Post-mitigation monitoring window; no residual error-rate change.
- Root cause hypothesis: recent autoscaler config change removed a lower-bound CPU request which allowed bursty tokenizer pods to co-locate, causing noisy-neighbor CPU contention on affected hosts.
- Immediate remediation: Rollback autoscaler change, re-introduce CPU request floor, and re-run canary.
- Next steps (action items): see Action Items section.

SLO snapshot (global) — morning sample at 06:00 UTC:
- gen-text 95p latency (global): 192ms (SLO target: 250ms)
- gen-text 99p latency (global): 410ms (SLO target: 500ms)
- embedding error-rate (7d): 0.12% (SLO target: 0.2%)
- eu-west gen-text 95p (peak during incident): 372ms (breach window ~23:14-00:26)
- Paging noise: 3 noisy alerts suppressed after initial triage (latency flapping around threshold).

Runbook / Playbook updates made during shift:
- tokenization-latency-playbook: clarified the autoscaler rollback steps and added a quickcheck script to surface per-node CPU steal metrics (added link to telemetry panels).
- added a short checklist for canary re-routing (who to notify in CS/Support).
- flagged tokenizer autoscaler PR template to require explicit CPU request floor for future changes.

On-call handoff notes (to morning shift):
- State: Primary mitigation applied; system stable but follow the 24h monitoring checklist for recurring regressions.
- Monitoring to watch: cpu.steal_pct by host (eu-west), gen-text 95p per-pool, tokenizer pod restart counts.
- Pending alerts: none open; one historical alert (R-INF-1723) in resolved state.
- Customer follow-up: CS flagged two dedicated customers worth outbound messaging if we see re-occurrence. Contact: @cs-lead (Slack).
- Escalations: None required.

Action Items (owners + expected dates):
- Aisha: Patch tokenizer autoscaler template and submit follow-up PR to infra -> due 2027-11-12 (PR draft created).
- Marcus: Run forensic host-level CPU steal sweep for gw-eu-* hosts and assemble a short summary -> due 2027-11-11 (ticket R-INF-1740).
- Elena: Draft customer note for CS review if we need to contact dedicated customers; include mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fix -> due 2027-11-13.
- Tom: Add canary routing playbook section into the rollout docs (Console -> Rollouts) and link to runbook -> due 2027-11-16.
- Ravi: Add a Grafana alert refinement ticket to reduce flapping (increase rolling window for eu-west 95p) -> due 2027-11-12.

Observability notes / lessons learned:
- Telemetry gap: per-host CPU steal metric existed but not surfaced on the immediate incident panel; moved to the top-level eu-west incident panel.
- Canary benefits: re-routing to quant-variant prevented customer-visible 5xx errors and reduced latency impact; note that automatic fallback rules may help in the future.
- Alert tuning: The 95p threshold worked but flapped during post-deploy churn; set a short restraint to avoid alert-fatigue (Ravi ticket).

Operational risks and upcoming maintenance:
- Risk: Increased EU traffic planned for Nov 15 test — recommend ensuring autoscaler templates validated across pools before that date.
- Scheduled work: Kernel patch window for a subset of host images in eu-west on Nov 12 (maintenance advisory sent to SRE list). Watch for scheduling side-effects.

Notes to self / informal jots (work-in-progress):
- Consider adding a cheap synthetic gen-text probe that runs tokenization-only path to detect tokenizer stalls earlier.
- We should capture a small heap/cgroup snapshot on affected hosts during next test window to reproduce CPU contention.
- Who on infra rotation is ok to approve a hotfix PR after hours? Need a short on-call approval matrix.

Appendix: Relevant tickets and links:
- R-INF-1723: Incident record (created 2027-11-09 23:18 UTC)
- R-INF-1730: Autoscaler rollback and mitigation (linked PR: infra/pull/287)
- R-INF-1740: Host forensic sweep (owner: Marcus Wu)
- Confluence: Ops Bridge Runbook (edited: tokenization-latency-playbook v1.2)

If anything else observed during handoff call, append below and tag owner.

-- End of shift notes (Aisha Patel, Ops Bridge lead)
